summary: Justified, safe merge of two independently reproduced row wins (c320 at full decode_1, about -3.7 us, and tiled pre-attention at SV32, about -1.0 to -1.4 us) onto master's per-kvhead (sliding decode_1 10.87 us). Prediction is about 1.53x (range 1.51-1.55), roughly 1% over the 1.5199 board entry, which is inside the CI. The per-shape rows and PATH CHOSEN lines show attribution directly, so no companion is needed. The one real hazard is a merge slip that silently brings back pre-per-kvhead sliding routing.
justification: A. The mechanism is measured, not inferred. Full decode_1, weight 16: master per-kvhead (4b608df5) is 22.70 us per shape (sk two-level 19.1 us plus pre-attention 1.4 us). c320 was 19.00 us in 52cbfaeb and 19.76 us in b9d062aa (splitkv_attn_kernel<320> 10.9 us, combine 4.4 us, pre-attention 1.3 us), and GATE A ratios of 0.894 and 0.892 reproduce across two builds. Per-kvhead touched only sliding code (sliding_cluster_kernel PERHEAD, _slide_*, and the _sd_setup_body route.pop(1)), and GATE A compares against the same two-level kernel, so the c320 ratio should carry over. SV32, weight 46: master is 28.83 us with untiled pre-attention at 4.2 us. Tiled runs measured 27.42 and 27.92 us, with _pre_attention_tiled_kernel at 2.3-2.6 us. Sliding decode_1, weight 46: per-kvhead is 10.87 us against 12.04 and 12.62 us in the two branches without it, and the merge keeps it. Arithmetic: the decode_1 load goes from 863.2 to about 804 weighted us (+7.4%), and the verify_32 load from 6167 to about 6102 (+1.06%). The geomean over 6 loads gives 1.5120 x 1.0120 x 1.0018, about 1.533x. The expected shapes and directions match the weights. Full decode_1 is still 4.4x its 4.3 us floor, so there is room left. The conjecture's L2 argument is moot rather than wrong: every shape is its own captured graph, timed from cold L2, so the two layers never share a graph. Weakest link: the SV32 piece is worth about 0.18% of headline, too small to show in the headline and only readable in its row (expect about 27.4-27.9 us against 28.83). The headline gain also rests almost entirely on c320, which is about 1.2%, so a run of 1.51-1.52 would be ambiguous at headline level without the rows. The second weak link is merge fidelity: 8 conflicts in setup and route orchestration.
confounders: sliding-decode1-cluster-per-kvhead (master 5d528bf3): disjoint shapes, but the same import orchestration. Its _sd_setup_body does route.pop(1, None) before freezing _SD_ROUTE, and _slide_init sets _SLIDE_PH. The regate branch snapshots and republishes _SD_ROUTE (_NB_SNAP, MappingProxyType(new_sd)). If that publish or restore is ported, it can overwrite or restore a table built without per-kvhead's changes. Since the neighbour regate is dropped, the port must not touch _SD_ROUTE at all. A wrong merge would show as sliding decode_1 at about 12 us instead of about 10.9 us, or as a missing 'PERHEAD ON' line.

full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (two-level sk kernel at FD1): this is the incumbent c320 replaces and the GATE A comparator. It is unchanged by per-kvhead, so the 0.89 ratio is not confounded. If GATE A falls back, the row stays at about 22.7 us.

fused-preattention-triton / paired-heads-launch-cleanup (master _pre_attention_kernel): the tiled kernel replaces this first node only at SV32 (unpaired, sliding). GATE B compares [tiled + rest] against [master + rest] on the merged master, so the gain is self-attributed.

restack-sliding-decode-sk-window-on-cluster-master (sk window at sliding decode B=17..32): regate's GATE B also probed SD32 tiled and kept master. Leaving every non-SV32 tiled class out keeps this untouched. Any SD32 movement would be noise or a merge error.
interference: No companion is warranted. Both ported pieces are shape-gated to rows that per-kvhead does not touch (FD1, SV32), and per-kvhead's only row (SD1) is kept unchanged. Each piece also prints its own PATH CHOSEN line with an in-run A/B ratio, and the profile shows which kernels ran per row. A gain or a loss can therefore be read row by row against three existing references: master 4b608df5 (FD1 22.70, SV32 28.83, SD1 10.87), regate 52cbfaeb (19.00 / 27.42 / 12.04) and naive b9d062aa (19.76 / 27.92 / 12.62). An ab-revert of per-kvhead would only reproduce 52cbfaeb. A control for c320 alone or SV32 alone would cost a scored run to learn what the row already shows.
rules_flags: None blocking. Routing flags (_NB_C320, _NB_TILED) are set once at import from config-shaped synthetic gates and only read in kernel_fn. Branching is on cfg class only, with no per-call mutable state and no global BLAS or backend toggles (grep of the regate patch finds none). This satisfies the standing policy.

_c320_forward allocates ws_acc, ws_ml and out with torch.empty sized from page_table.shape[1] and batch. These are shape-derived, not value-derived, the same pattern master uses, and fine under graph capture.
c320 reads every key: it splits the full context into 320-token chunks with no skipping. Queries are FP8 e4m3, which is allowed. The cache write stays in master's pre-attention kernel.

Time budget: regate's import finished at +189.3 s with its full regate phase set. This merge adds per-kvhead's PERHEAD build but drops most regate phases, so it should stay well within 480 s and 15 min. The builder must keep the c320 load_inline strictly sequential, after every master build including _slide_ph_init. A concurrent load_inline would race torch's build dir and ninja locks.
open_questions: Builder checklist for the 8-conflict merge: (1) do not port the _SD_ROUTE publish or snapshot entries, or the neighbour-regate phases P4 and P6. (2) Confirm the log shows '[slide] PATH CHOSEN: sliding B=1 PERHEAD ON', 'PATH CHOSEN: full decode_1 [A chunk320]: route (... ratio <= 0.98)', and 'GATE B SV32: tiled first node', with every other GATE B class on master. (3) Run okc-style local lint, and if possible a local import, to confirm the 480 s start rule and fallback paths.

Readout rule for the scored run: success means FD1 at about 19-19.8 us, SV32 at about 27.4-27.9 us, and SD1 at about 10.9 us. If the headline lands inside [1.497, 1.543] but those rows hold, the stacking conjecture is confirmed even though the headline is not a statistically proven best. If SD1 is about 12 us, the merge reverted per-kvhead routing; that is a build error, not a result.

Bookkeeping: BEST.json lists score_us 2490.98 and CI [1.4893, 1.5347], which are master 4b608df5's numbers, against job 52cbfaeb, whose own values are 2477.92 and [1.4971, 1.5427]. Fix this before comparing the merge to the board.

No scored test covers full decode at B=1 (the tests cover B=4 full decode and B=1/2 full verify). The c320 path is exercised only by GATE A and by the scored shape's per-call reference check. Both of those passed twice, but a c320 regression would surface only at the scored shape.
